name: Amitriptyline

fields.mechanism_of_action: Amitriptyline hydrochloride is a tricyclic antidepressant with sedative effects. Its mechanism of action in man is not known. It is not a monoamine oxidase inhibitor and it does not act primarily by stimulation of the central nervous system. Amitriptyline inhibits the membrane pump mechanism responsible for uptake of norepinephrine and serotonin in adrenergic and serotonergic neurons; pharmacologically this action may potentiate or prolong neuronal activity, since reuptake of these biogenic amines is important physiologically in terminating transmitting activity. This interference with reuptake of norepinephrine and/or serotonin is believed by some to underlie the antidepressant activity of amitriptyline (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY).
indications: Relief of symptoms of depression. Endogenous depression is more likely to be alleviated than are other depressive states (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, INDICATIONS AND USAGE; ELAVIL label, INDICATIONS AND USAGE).
Amitriptyline is not approved for use in pediatric patients (ELAVIL label, boxed warning text and Precautions: Pediatric Use).
contraindications: Prior hypersensitivity to amitriptyline hydrochloride (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, CONTRAINDICATIONS).

Concomitant use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors: hyperpyretic crises, severe convulsions and deaths have occurred in patients receiving tricyclic antidepressant and monoamine oxidase inhibiting drugs simultaneously. When it is desired to replace a monoamine oxidase inhibitor with amitriptyline hydrochloride, a minimum of 14 days should be allowed to elapse after the former is discontinued, and amitriptyline should then be initiated cautiously with gradual increase in dosage until optimum response is achieved (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, CONTRAINDICATIONS and WARNINGS: Serotonin Syndrome).
Concomitant use with cisapride, due to the potential for increased QT interval and increased risk of arrhythmia (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, CONTRAINDICATIONS).
Not recommended for use during the acute recovery phase following myocardial infarction (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, CONTRAINDICATIONS).
side_effects: Cardiovascular: myocardial infarction, stroke, nonspecific ECG changes and changes in AV conduction, heart block, arrhythmias, hypotension (particularly orthostatic hypotension), syncope, hypertension, tachycardia and palpitation (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Central nervous system and neuromuscular: coma, seizures, hallucinations, delusions, confusional states, disorientation, incoordination, ataxia, tremors, peripheral neuropathy, numbness, tingling and paresthesias of the extremities, extrapyramidal symptoms including abnormal involuntary movements and tardive dyskinesia, dysarthria, disturbed concentration, excitement, anxiety, insomnia, restlessness, nightmares, drowsiness, dizziness, weakness, fatigue, headache, syndrome of inappropriate ADH secretion, tinnitus and alteration in EEG patterns (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Anticholinergic: paralytic ileus, hyperpyrexia, urinary retention and dilatation of the urinary tract, constipation, blurred vision, disturbance of accommodation, increased intraocular pressure, mydriasis and dry mouth (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
Allergic: skin rash, urticaria, photosensitization, and edema of face and tongue (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
Hematologic: bone marrow depression including agranulocytosis, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, purpura and eosinophilia (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Gastrointestinal: rarely hepatitis (including altered liver function and jaundice), nausea, epigastric distress, vomiting, anorexia, stomatitis, peculiar taste, diarrhea, parotid swelling and black tongue (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Endocrine: testicular swelling and gynecomastia in the male, breast enlargement and galactorrhea in the female, increased or decreased libido, impotence, and elevation and lowering of blood sugar levels (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
Other: alopecia, edema, weight gain or loss, urinary frequency, increased perspiration and hyponatremia (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Withdrawal symptoms: after prolonged administration, abrupt cessation of treatment may produce nausea, headache and malaise; gradual dosage reduction has been reported to produce, within two weeks, transient symptoms including irritability, restlessness and dream and sleep disturbance. These symptoms are not indicative of addiction (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Post-marketing: a syndrome resembling neuroleptic malignant syndrome has been very rarely reported after starting or increasing the dose of amitriptyline, with muscle rigidity, fever, mental status changes, diaphoresis, tachycardia and tremor; very rare cases of serotonin syndrome have been reported in combination with other drugs associated with serotonin syndrome, and very rare cases of cardiomyopathy (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS: Post-marketing Adverse Events).

dosage.adult: Oral (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION): dosage should be initiated at a low level and increased gradually, noting carefully the clinical response and any evidence of intolerance. For outpatients, 75 mg/day in divided doses is usually satisfactory; if necessary this may be increased to a total of 150 mg per day, with increases made preferably in the late afternoon and/or bedtime doses. A sedative effect may be apparent before the antidepressant effect is noted, and an adequate therapeutic effect may take as long as 30 days to develop. An alternate method is to begin with 50 mg to 100 mg at bedtime, increasing by 25 mg or 50 mg as necessary in the bedtime dose to a total of 150 mg per day. Hospitalized patients may require 100 mg/day initially, which can be increased gradually to 200 mg/day if necessary; a small number of hospitalized patients may need as much as 300 mg/day. Maintenance: the usual maintenance dosage is 50 mg to 100 mg per day; in some patients 40 mg per day is sufficient; for maintenance the total daily dose may be given as a single dose, preferably at bedtime. When satisfactory improvement has been reached, the dose should be reduced to the lowest amount that will maintain relief of symptoms, and it is appropriate to continue maintenance therapy 3 months or longer to lessen the possibility of relapse.
dosage.geriatric: Clinical experience has not identified differences in responses between elderly and younger patients; in general, dose selection for an elderly patient should be cautious, usually starting at the low end of the dosing range, reflecting the greater frequency of decreased hepatic function, concomitant disease and other drug therapy. Geriatric patients are particularly sensitive to the anticholinergic side effects of tricyclic antidepressants including amitriptyline - peripheral anticholinergic effects include tachycardia, urinary retention, constipation, dry mouth, blurred vision and exacerbation of narrow angle glaucoma, and central nervous system anticholinergic effects include cognitive impairment, psychomotor slowing, confusion, sedation and delirium. Elderly patients taking amitriptyline may be at increased risk for falls, should be started on low doses and observed closely. As a general rule, lower dosages are recommended for elderly patients: 10 mg three times a day with 20 mg at bedtime may be satisfactory in elderly patients who do not tolerate higher dosages (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS: Geriatric Use and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).
dosage.paediatric: In view of the lack of experience with the use of this drug in pediatric patients, it is not recommended at the present time for patients under 12 years of age, and safety and effectiveness in the pediatric population have not been established (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION: Pediatric Use and PRECAUTIONS: Pediatric Use). The ELAVIL boxed warning states that anyone considering the use of amitriptyline in a child, adolescent or young adult must balance the potential risk of suicidality with the clinical need.

interactions: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors: contraindicated - see CONTRAINDICATIONS. Amitriptyline should not be started in a patient being treated with MAOIs such as linezolid or intravenous methylene blue, and amitriptyline should be discontinued before initiating such an MAOI (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, CONTRAINDICATIONS and WARNINGS: Serotonin Syndrome).

Other serotonergic drugs: the development of a potentially life-threatening serotonin syndrome has been reported with tricyclic antidepressants, including amitriptyline, alone but particularly with concomitant use of other serotonergic drugs (including triptans, tricyclic antidepressants, SSRI/SNRI, fentanyl, lithium, tramadol, tryptophan, buspirone and St John's Wort) and with drugs that impair metabolism of serotonin (in particular MAOIs, linezolid and intravenous methylene blue). Treatment with amitriptyline and any concomitant serotonergic agent should be discontinued immediately if serotonin syndrome occurs and supportive symptomatic treatment initiated (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Serotonin Syndrome).
Cisapride: should not be given with amitriptyline due to the potential for increased QT interval and increased risk of arrhythmia (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, CONTRAINDICATIONS).

Topiramate: some patients may experience a large increase in amitriptyline concentration; any adjustment of the amitriptyline dose should be made according to the patient's clinical response and not on the basis of plasma levels (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions).

Drugs metabolized by cytochrome P450 2D6: about 7% to 10% of Caucasians are poor metabolizers and have higher than expected plasma concentrations of tricyclic antidepressants at usual doses, with an increase in plasma AUC that may be small or quite large (up to 8-fold). Drugs that inhibit P450 2D6 include quinidine and cimetidine (not metabolized by the enzyme) and many P450 2D6 substrates including other antidepressants, phenothiazines and the type 1C antiarrhythmics propafenone and flecainide; SSRIs such as fluoxetine, sertraline and paroxetine also inhibit P450 2D6 to varying extents. Co-administration may require lower doses than usually prescribed for either drug, and an increased amitriptyline dose may be required when the inhibiting drug is withdrawn; TCA plasma levels should be monitored during co-administration. At least 5 weeks may be necessary before initiating TCA treatment in a patient being withdrawn from fluoxetine, given its long half-life (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions).

Guanethidine or similarly acting compounds: amitriptyline may block the antihypertensive action of guanethidine or similarly acting compounds (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Screening Patients for Bipolar Disorder and PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions).

Thyroid medication: close supervision is required when amitriptyline is given to hyperthyroid patients or those receiving thyroid medication (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Screening Patients for Bipolar Disorder and PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions).

Alcohol, barbiturates and other CNS depressants: amitriptyline may enhance the response to alcohol and the effects of barbiturates and other CNS depressants, increasing the danger inherent in any suicide attempt or overdosage; delirium has been reported with concurrent administration of amitriptyline and disulfiram (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Screening Patients for Bipolar Disorder and PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions).

Anticholinergic agents and sympathomimetic drugs, including epinephrine combined with local anaesthetics: close supervision and careful adjustment of dosages are required. Hyperpyrexia has been reported when amitriptyline is administered with anticholinergic agents or with neuroleptic drugs, particularly during hot weather, and paralytic ileus may occur with tricyclic antidepressants in combination with anticholinergic-type drugs (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions).

Cimetidine: reduces hepatic metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants, delaying elimination and increasing steady-state concentrations, with increases in plasma levels and in the frequency and severity of side effects, particularly anticholinergic effects (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions).

Ethchlorvynol: caution is advised with large concurrent doses - transient delirium has been reported in patients treated with one gram of ethchlorvynol and 75 mg to 150 mg of amitriptyline (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions).
fields.monitoring: Because of the wide variation in the absorption and distribution of tricyclic antidepressants in body fluids it is difficult to directly correlate plasma levels and therapeutic effect; however, plasma level determination may be useful in identifying patients who appear to have toxic effects and may have excessively high levels, or those in whom lack of absorption or non-compliance is suspected. Because of increased intestinal transit time and decreased hepatic metabolism in elderly patients, plasma levels are generally higher for a given oral dose in elderly patients than in younger patients; elderly patients should be monitored carefully and quantitative serum levels obtained as clinically appropriate, and dosage adjustments should be made according to the patient's clinical response and not on the basis of plasma levels (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION: Plasma Levels). Monitor closely for clinical worsening, suicidality and unusual changes in behaviour, especially early in treatment and after dose changes, and monitor patients with cardiovascular disorders closely for arrhythmias, sinus tachycardia and prolongation of conduction time (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Clinical Worsening and Suicide Risk and Screening Patients for Bipolar Disorder). Watch for the emergence of serotonin syndrome, particularly during treatment initiation and dose increases (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Serotonin Syndrome). In patients with symptomatic hyponatremia, discontinue amitriptyline and institute appropriate medical intervention, with greater risk in elderly patients, patients taking diuretics and those who are volume-depleted (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Hyponatremia).
fields.patient_counselling: Patients, families and caregivers should be encouraged to be alert to the emergence of anxiety, agitation, panic attacks, insomnia, irritability, hostility, aggressiveness, impulsivity, akathisia (psychomotor restlessness), hypomania, mania, other unusual changes in behaviour, worsening of depression and suicidal ideation, especially early during antidepressant treatment and when the dose is adjusted up or down; changes can be abrupt and should be reported to the prescriber, as they may indicate an increased risk of suicidal thinking and behavior and require very close monitoring and possibly changes in medication (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS: Information for Patients and WARNINGS: Clinical Worsening and Suicide Risk; Medication Guide). Advise patients of the possible impairment of mental and/or physical abilities required for the performance of hazardous tasks, such as operating machinery or driving a motor vehicle (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS: Information for Patients). Advise patients that amitriptyline can cause mild pupillary dilation, which in susceptible individuals can lead to an episode of angle-closure glaucoma; patients with pre-existing open-angle glaucoma are not at risk, but susceptible patients may wish to be examined to determine susceptibility and have a prophylactic procedure such as iridectomy if necessary (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS: Information for Patients and WARNINGS: Angle-Closure Glaucoma). Advise patients never to stop an antidepressant medicine without first talking to a healthcare provider, because stopping abruptly can cause other symptoms (Medication Guide). Advise patients to watch for low sodium symptoms - headache, weakness or feeling unsteady, confusion, problems concentrating, thinking or memory problems - and for visual problems (eye pain, changes in vision, swelling or redness in or around the eye) and for serotonin syndrome symptoms (agitation, hallucinations, coma or other changes in mental status; racing heartbeat, high or low blood pressure; coordination problems or muscle twitching; nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea; sweating or fever; muscle rigidity) (Medication Guide). The prescriber or health professional should instruct patients, their families and caregivers to read the Medication Guide and assist them in understanding its contents (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS: Information for Patients).
warnings: WARNING (boxed): Suicidality and Antidepressant Drugs. Antidepressants increased the risk compared to placebo of suicidal thinking and behavior (suicidality) in children, adolescents and young adults in short-term studies of major depressive disorder (MDD) and other psychiatric disorders. Anyone considering the use of amitriptyline hydrochloride tablets or any other antidepressant in a child, adolescent or young adult must balance this risk with the clinical need. Short-term studies did not show an increase in the risk of suicidality with antidepressants compared to placebo in adults beyond age 24; there was a reduction in risk compared to placebo in adults aged 65 and older. Patients of all ages who are started on antidepressant therapy should be monitored appropriately and observed closely for clinical worsening, suicidality, or unusual changes in behavior. Families and caregivers should be advised of the need for close observation and communication with the prescriber. Amitriptyline hydrochloride tablets are not approved for use in pediatric patients (ELAVIL label, boxed warning).

Clinical worsening and suicide risk: pooled analyses of short-term placebo-controlled trials showed antidepressants increase the risk of suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents and young adults (ages 18 to 24) with MDD and other psychiatric disorders, with a drug-placebo difference of 14 additional cases per 1,000 patients treated under 18 and 5 additional cases per 1,000 in the 18 to 24 age range, versus 1 fewer case per 1,000 at ages 25 to 64 and 6 fewer cases per 1,000 at 65 and older (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Clinical Worsening and Suicide Risk, Table 1).

Serotonin syndrome: a potentially life-threatening serotonin syndrome has been reported with tricyclic antidepressants, including amitriptyline, alone but particularly with concomitant serotonergic drugs and drugs that impair metabolism of serotonin; symptoms may include mental status changes (agitation, hallucinations, delirium, coma), autonomic instability (tachycardia, labile blood pressure, dizziness, diaphoresis, flushing, hyperthermia), neuromuscular changes (tremor, rigidity, myoclonus, hyperreflexia, incoordination), seizures and/or gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea) (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Serotonin Syndrome).

Screening patients for bipolar disorder: a major depressive episode may be the initial presentation of bipolar disorder, and treating such an episode with an antidepressant alone may increase the likelihood of precipitation of a mixed/manic episode in patients at risk; prior to initiating treatment patients should be adequately screened for bipolar disorder, including a detailed psychiatric history with family history of suicide, bipolar disorder and depression. Amitriptyline is not approved for use in treating bipolar depression (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Screening Patients for Bipolar Disorder).

Hyponatremia: has occurred as a result of treatment with amitriptyline, in many cases as a result of the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion; symptoms include headache, difficulty concentrating, memory impairment, confusion, weakness and unsteadiness, which may lead to falls, with more severe or acute cases including syncope, seizure, coma, respiratory arrest and death. In patients with symptomatic hyponatremia, discontinue amitriptyline and institute appropriate medical intervention (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Hyponatremia).

Angle-closure glaucoma: the pupillary dilation that occurs following use of many antidepressant drugs including amitriptyline may trigger an angle closure attack in a patient with anatomically narrow angles who does not have a patent iridectomy (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Angle-Closure Glaucoma).

Cardiovascular: patients with cardiovascular disorders should be watched closely; tricyclic antidepressant drugs, including amitriptyline, particularly when given in high doses, have been reported to produce arrhythmias, sinus tachycardia and prolongation of conduction time, and myocardial infarction and stroke have been reported with drugs of this class (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Screening Patients for Bipolar Disorder).
Seizures: use with caution in patients with a history of seizures (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Screening Patients for Bipolar Disorder).

Anticholinergic effects: because of its atropine-like action, use with caution in patients with a history of urinary retention, angle closure glaucoma or increased intraocular pressure; in patients with angle closure glaucoma even average doses may precipitate an attack (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Screening Patients for Bipolar Disorder).

Hyperthyroidism: close supervision is required when amitriptyline is given to hyperthyroid patients or those receiving thyroid medication (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Screening Patients for Bipolar Disorder).
precautions: Schizophrenic patients may develop increased symptoms of psychosis, and patients with paranoid symptomatology may have an exaggeration of such symptoms; depressed patients, particularly those with known manic-depressive illness, may experience a shift to mania or hypomania, in which circumstances the dose of amitriptyline may be reduced or a major tranquilizer such as perphenazine administered concurrently (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS).

The possibility of suicide in depressed patients remains until significant remission occurs; potentially suicidal patients should not have access to large quantities of the drug, and prescriptions should be written for the smallest amount feasible (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS).

Concurrent administration of amitriptyline and electroshock therapy may increase the hazards associated with such therapy, and such treatment should be limited to patients for whom it is essential (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS).
When possible, the drug should be discontinued several days before elective surgery (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS).

Both elevation and lowering of blood sugar levels have been reported, and amitriptyline should be used with caution in patients with impaired liver function (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS).

Amitriptyline may enhance the response to alcohol and the effects of barbiturates and other CNS depressants; in patients who may use alcohol excessively, the potentiation may increase the danger inherent in any suicide attempt or overdosage (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Screening Patients for Bipolar Disorder).

Rare instances of mania or hypomania have been reported within 2 to 7 days following cessation of chronic therapy with tricyclic antidepressants (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS: Withdrawal Symptoms).

Causal relationship unknown reactions reported under circumstances where a causal relationship could not be established include lupus-like syndrome (migratory arthritis, positive ANA and rheumatoid factor), hepatic failure and ageusia (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS: Causal Relationship Unknown).

Dispense in a tight, light-resistant container as defined in the USP using a child-resistant closure, and dispense a Medication Guide with each prescription (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, HOW SUPPLIED).
serious_adverse_reactions: Suicidality and suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents and young adults (boxed warning) (ELAVIL label, boxed warning; Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Clinical Worsening and Suicide Risk).
Serotonin syndrome, potentially life-threatening (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Serotonin Syndrome).
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome-like syndrome (very rarely reported) (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS: Post-marketing Adverse Events).

Cardiac dysrhythmias, heart block, myocardial infarction and stroke, particularly at high doses and in patients with cardiovascular disorders (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS and ADVERSE REACTIONS).
Seizures and status epilepticus in overdose (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS and OVERDOSAGE).
Hyponatraemia with syncope, seizure, coma, respiratory arrest and death (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Hyponatremia).
Bone marrow depression including agranulocytosis, leukopenia and thrombocytopenia (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
Paralytic ileus and hyperpyrexia from anticholinergic effects (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS and PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions).
Acute angle-closure glaucoma (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Angle-Closure Glaucoma).
Hepatitis with altered liver function and jaundice (rare) (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, ADVERSE REACTIONS).
fields.pregnancy_category: C (ELAVIL label, PRECAUTIONS: Usage in Pregnancy). FDA pregnancy categories are obsolete and are reported here only because the label still states them.
fields.pregnancy_guidance: Teratogenic effects were not observed in mice, rats or rabbits when amitriptyline was given orally at doses of 2 to 40 mg/kg/day (up to 13 times the maximum recommended human dose); studies in the literature have shown amitriptyline to be teratogenic in mice and hamsters at 28 to 100 mg/kg/day (9 to 33 times the maximum recommended human dose), producing multiple malformations, and in rats an oral dose of 25 mg/kg/day produced delays of ossification of fetal vertebral bodies; in rabbits an oral dose of 60 mg/kg/day caused incomplete ossification of the cranial bones. Amitriptyline has been shown to cross the placenta, and although a causal relationship has not been established, there have been a few reports of adverse events, including CNS effects, limb deformities or developmental delay, in infants whose mothers had taken amitriptyline during pregnancy. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women, and amitriptyline should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit to the mother justifies the potential risk to the fetus (ELAVIL label, PRECAUTIONS: Usage in Pregnancy; Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Pregnancy).
fields.lactation_guidance: Amitriptyline is excreted into breast milk. In one report in which a patient received amitriptyline 100 mg/day while nursing her infant, levels of 83 to 141 ng/mL were detected in the mother's serum and levels of 135 to 151 ng/mL were found in the breast milk, but no trace of the drug could be detected in the infant's serum. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants from amitriptyline, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or to discontinue the drug, taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother (ELAVIL label, PRECAUTIONS: Nursing Mothers; Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Nursing Mothers).
fields.overdose: Deaths may occur from overdosage with tricyclic antidepressant class drugs, and multiple drug ingestion (including alcohol) is common in deliberate overdose; because the management is complex and changing, it is recommended that the physician contact a poison control center for current information on treatment. Signs and symptoms of toxicity develop rapidly, so hospital monitoring is required as soon as possible. Critical manifestations include cardiac dysrhythmias, severe hypotension, convulsions and CNS depression including coma; changes in the electrocardiogram, particularly in QRS axis or width, are clinically significant indicators of toxicity, and a rightward axis shift in the terminal QRS complex together with a prolonged QT interval and sinus tachycardia are specific and sensitive indicators of first generation tricyclic overdose. Management: obtain an ECG and immediately initiate cardiac monitoring, protect the airway, establish intravenous access and initiate gastric decontamination, with a minimum of six hours of observation with cardiac monitoring. All patients suspected of overdose should receive gastrointestinal decontamination with large volume gastric lavage followed by activated charcoal; EMESIS IS CONTRAINDICATED. A maximal limb lead QRS duration of 0.10 seconds or more may be the best indication of the severity of the overdose; intravenous sodium bicarbonate should be used to maintain serum pH 7.45 to 7.55, with hyperventilation used if the pH response is inadequate, and dysrhythmias unresponsive to these measures may respond to lidocaine, bretylium or phenytoin; type 1A and 1C antiarrhythmics are generally contraindicated (e.g. quinidine, disopyramide and procainamide). In patients with CNS depression, early intubation is advised because of the potential for abrupt deterioration, and seizures should be controlled with benzodiazepines or, if ineffective, other anticonvulsants such as phenobarbital or phenytoin. Physostigmine is not recommended except for life-threatening symptoms unresponsive to other therapies and then only in consultation with a poison control center. Since overdosage is often deliberate, patients may attempt suicide by other means during the recovery phase and psychiatric referral may be appropriate (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, OVERDOSAGE).
fields.pharmacokinetics: Studies in man following oral administration of 14C-labeled drug indicated that amitriptyline is rapidly absorbed and metabolized; radioactivity of the plasma was practically negligible, although significant amounts of radioactivity appeared in the urine by 4 to 6 hours and one-half to one-third of the drug was excreted within 24 hours. Amitriptyline is metabolized by N-demethylation and bridge hydroxylation in man, rabbit and rat; virtually the entire dose is excreted as glucuronide or sulfate conjugate of metabolites, with little unchanged drug appearing in the urine, and other metabolic pathways may be involved. Because of the wide variation in the absorption and distribution of tricyclic antidepressants in body fluids it is difficult to directly correlate plasma levels and therapeutic effect. Approximately 7% to 10% of Caucasians are poor metabolizers of cytochrome P450 2D6 and have higher than expected plasma concentrations of tricyclic antidepressants at usual doses, with increases in plasma AUC that may be small or up to 8-fold (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, HOW SUPPLIED: METABOLISM and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION: Plasma Levels; PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions).
clinical_pearls: Amitriptyline is one of the most sedating and most anticholinergic tricyclic antidepressants: dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision, tachycardia and confusion are dose-related and are the dominant adverse effects in older patients, who should be started on low doses and observed closely (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS: Geriatric Use and ADVERSE REACTIONS).

Suicidality risk is age-dependent: in pooled placebo-controlled trials the excess risk of suicidal thinking and behaviour was 14 additional cases per 1,000 patients treated under 18 and 5 per 1,000 at ages 18-24, with no excess beyond age 24 and a reduction in adults aged 65 and older (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Clinical Worsening and Suicide Risk, Table 1).

Screen for bipolar disorder before treating a major depressive episode with an antidepressant alone, because antidepressant monotherapy can precipitate mixed or manic episodes; amitriptyline is not approved for bipolar depression (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, WARNINGS: Screening Patients for Bipolar Disorder).

Amitriptyline is not for acute use: an adequate therapeutic effect may take as long as 30 days to develop, and the sedative effect usually precedes the antidepressant effect (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).

The 14-day rule with MAOIs applies in both directions - hyperpyretic crises, severe convulsions and deaths have occurred with concomitant use, and at least 14 days must elapse after stopping an MAOI before starting amitriptyline (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, CONTRAINDICATIONS).

Serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs is amplified by P450 2D6 inhibition; after stopping fluoxetine, wait at least 5 weeks before starting a TCA because of the long half-life of fluoxetine and norfluoxetine (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions).

Switching between classes is a two-way risk: an SSRI inhibits P450 2D6 and can make a previously stable TCA dose toxic, and stopping the inhibitor can require an increase in TCA dose, so monitor TCA plasma levels (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS: Drug Interactions).

Overdose is a medical emergency with characteristic ECG findings: QRS widening, rightward axis shift, prolonged QT and sinus tachycardia; treat with sodium bicarbonate to maintain pH 7.45-7.55 and benzodiazepines for seizures, and never induce emesis (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, OVERDOSAGE).
Discontinue several days before elective surgery where possible (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS).
black_box_warnings: Suicidality and Antidepressant Drugs. Antidepressants increased the risk compared to placebo of suicidal thinking and behavior (suicidality) in children, adolescents, and young adults in short-term studies of major depressive disorder (MDD) and other psychiatric disorders. Anyone considering the use of amitriptyline hydrochloride tablets or any other antidepressant in a child, adolescent, or young adult must balance this risk with the clinical need. Short-term studies did not show an increase in the risk of suicidality with antidepressants compared to placebo in adults beyond age 24; there was a reduction in risk with antidepressants compared to placebo in adults aged 65 and older. Depression and certain other psychiatric disorders are themselves associated with increases in the risk of suicide. Patients of all ages who are started on antidepressant therapy should be monitored appropriately and observed closely for clinical worsening, suicidality, or unusual changes in behavior. Families and caregivers should be advised of the need for close observation and communication with the prescriber. Amitriptyline hydrochloride tablets are not approved for use in pediatric patients (ELAVIL label, boxed warning).
fields.hepatic_dose_adjustment: No hepatic dose adjustment is specified in the label. The label does state that amitriptyline should be used with caution in patients with impaired liver function, and that rarely hepatitis (including altered liver function and jaundice) has been reported (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, PRECAUTIONS and ADVERSE REACTIONS).
fields.administration_instructions: Oral. Initiate at a low level and increase gradually, noting carefully the clinical response and any evidence of intolerance; for outpatients start at 75 mg/day in divided doses or 50 mg to 100 mg at bedtime, increasing as needed to a total of 150 mg/day, with increases made preferably in the late afternoon and/or bedtime doses; for maintenance, the total daily dose may be given as a single dose preferably at bedtime, reduced to the lowest amount that maintains relief of symptoms, and continued for 3 months or longer (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION). Tablets are available in 25 mg, 50 mg, 75 mg, 100 mg and 150 mg strengths; store at 20 to 25 degrees C (68 to 77 degrees F), protect from light, dispense in a tight, light-resistant container using a child-resistant closure, and dispense a Medication Guide with each prescription (Amitriptyline Hydrochloride tablets label, HOW SUPPLIED).

notes: The table stores this agent as 'Amitriptyline'; the US label names are amitriptyline hydrochloride tablets, with the historic brand ELAVIL. The main content is taken from a current FDA-approved generic amitriptyline hydrochloride tablet label (Aurobindo), and the boxed warning ('Suicidality and Antidepressant Drugs') and the Pregnancy Category C statement are taken from the ELAVIL label, whose legacy SPL carries the boxed warning text explicitly whereas the modern generic SPL references a boxed warning that is not itself included. Note that the generic label's WARNINGS section contains a caveat that the clinical worsening and suicidality pooled analyses were derived from 24 short-term trials of 9 antidepressant drugs in over 4,400 paediatric/adolescent patients and 295 short-term trials of 11 antidepressant drugs in over 77,000 adults; these are class-level pooled figures and are labelled as such here. FDA pregnancy category C is obsolete (replaced by the Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule) and is reported only because the label still states it. The database brand_names field lists 'Amitriptyline Hydrochloride', which is the generic product name rather than a brand; the verified brand product Elavil has been recorded here instead.
